abstract: While bride price customs are widespread in many developing countries, little is known about their consequences on men’s decisions. In this paper, we exploit a quasi-natural experiment of a school-building program in Indonesia (INPRES) to investigate the relationship between marriage norms and the internal migrations of young men. Combining anthropological, administrative, and individual-based datasets, we implement a triple-difference approach. We show that the less advantaged young men, who have fewer resources to cope with rising marriage costs, are more likely to migrate out of their district of origin when the women they are expected to marry benefit from the program. These findings suggest that the interaction between marital norms and policies can result in unintended consequences, shaping major economic decisions such as premarital migration.
title: Premarital migration and marriage payments: Evidence from Indonesian men

abstract: The two most prominent strategy-proof school choice mechanisms, Deferred Acceptance and Top Trading Cycles, offer a trade-off between eliminating justified-envy and Pareto efficiency, respectively. We introduce a novel, biometric approach to investigate how much individuals care about and physiologically react to each property. Using an experimental design that randomly varies whether subjects learn about others’ assignments in a school choice game, we measure arousal through galvanic skin response and valence through facial expressions when subjects experience envy with and without justification. We find increased arousal associated with receiving successively lower-ranked allocations, i.e., the (unjustified) envy of the allocation(s) of others. We note additional arousal when that envy is justified, but that result requires an explicit message to accentuate the justification. Eye-tracking data confirm that subjects do not notice markers of justified-envy until receiving this message. Facial-expression valence yields less conclusive results, but this may be due to the limitations of that method for anger detection.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization
title: Biometric responses to unjustified and justified-envy in school choice allocations

abstract: We show that cross-border learning is an important feature of modern semiconductor manufacturing and that several important channels - such as knowledge sharing along global supply chains, the movement of engineers within multinational firms, and foreign direct investment - operate through market mechanisms rather than anonymous technological spillovers. These findings have significant policy implications. When cross-border learning is mediated by purposeful economic relationships, access to frontier knowledge is neither automatic nor guaranteed. Firms and governments can facilitate - or restrict - the international diffusion of technology, implying that policies to foster domestic technological upgrading are likely to be most effective when coupled with continued access to global sources of frontier knowledge.

abstract: The value of lawyers to their clients is notoriously difficult to estimate because of endogeneity. We utilize modifications to the collateral source (CS) rule that require reducing trial awards by the amount of payments from first‐party insurance as an instrument for hiring a lawyer. The problem with our instrument is that modifications to the CS rule have a direct effect on recovery and, hence, violate the exclusion restriction required for a valid instrument. We develop a new identification and estimation method that uses CS rule changes as an invalid instrument and bounds the impact of lawyers. We find that our estimated impact's upper and lower bounds are lower than estimates that do not correct for endogeneity. Our estimates of the impact of lawyers on total payment are consistently negative, although not precise enough to claim statistical significance. The upper bound of the effect of hiring a lawyer on total payment received is negative after fees in our preferred specification. This suggests that even in the most optimistic scenario, lawyers appear to reduce total recovery.
title: The Value of an Attorney: Collateral Source Rule Changes as an Invalid Instrument

abstract: Does the National Treatment (NT) principle inevitably induce "hidden green protectionism"? While existing literature suggests that NT leads to inefficiently stringent product standards, we show that this distortion vanishes when governments can jointly deploy standards and internal taxes. Using an international oligopoly model, we find that the threshold for switching to cleaner standards under NT coincides with that under international cooperation. The availability of internal fiscal instruments allows governments to decouple environmental objectives from strategic trade motives, thereby restoring the regulatory efficiency of standard-setting under NT.
title: Neutralizing Hidden Green Protectionism: The Efficiency of National Treatment with Internal Taxes

abstract: Governments have adopted various climate policies to decarbonize their electricity sectors, and several cross-national studies find that pricing, regulatory, and subsidy measures are associated with emissions reductions. However, such aggregate estimates implicitly assume that power plants' emissions are equally responsive to climate instruments. We examine whether ownership structures condition associations between national climate policies and plants' CO2 emissions. Using a global dataset covering 13,661 fossil-fueled power plants across 134 countries, linked to harmonized measures of policy adoption, stringency, duration, and policy mixes, we find that climate policies are significantly more strongly associated with lower CO2 emissions among investor-owned plants than among state-owned plants across these four dimensions of policy exposure. This is especially true of carbon taxes, emissions trading schemes, fossil-fuel subsidy reform, air-pollution standards, coal bans and phase-outs, renewable planning, and renewable auctions. State-owned plants’ emissions are negatively related to a much narrower set of policies, most notably renewable portfolio standards, while several policies are either unrelated to or positively associated with their emissions. These results suggest that evaluating climate policy solely at the sectoral level can overlook important institutional differences in how policies are implemented. In particular, future policies must account for how state-owned enterprises interpret and translate policy signals into actual emissions outcomes.
title: Ownership structures shape climate-policy effectiveness in electricity generation

abstract: Egypt and Brazil are among the developing countries receiving the highest levels of international finance for clean energy; yet, they differ substantially in their renewable energy potential, energy composition, and policy frameworks, allowing for a comparative analysis of how these factors affect the development of low-carbon energy. This study examines the impact of environmental taxes, international finance received for clean energy, government expenditures, green innovation, and ecological footprint on low-carbon energy in Egypt and Brazil from 2000 to 2022. The robust results indicate that environmental taxes have a positive influence on low-carbon energy in Brazil. In contrast, international finance for clean energy has a positive effect in Brazil but an adverse effect in Egypt. Government expenditures negatively impact low-carbon energy in Egypt, whereas the ecological footprint exhibits a negative effect in Brazil. These findings suggest that the effectiveness of international finance and government expenditures critically depends on domestic energy structures, renewable energy potential, and the allocation of fiscal resources. In Brazil, established renewable infrastructure and diversified energy sources support the positive impact of international finance for clean energy. In Egypt, reliance on fossil fuels and limited deployment of renewables may reduce the effectiveness of external funding. The results indicate that aligning financial and fiscal measures with renewable energy expansion and low-carbon strategies.
title: The impact of international clean energy finance and public policies on the low-carbon energy transition: Evidence from Egypt and Brazil

abstract: A set-aside promotes a more equitable procurement process by restricting participation in government tenders to small or disadvantaged businesses. Yet its micro-effects on tender outcomes (competition and contract efficiency) and targeted firm performance entail trade-offs, which we evaluate empirically using a decade of US federal procurement data. At the tender level, we employ a two-stage approach. First, we use random forest techniques to compute the propensity score for a tender being set aside based on rules implementation. Second, we employ the scores in an inverse probability weighting framework. We find that set-asides prompt more competition — implying that the rise in participation of targeted firms more than offsets the exclusion of untargeted ones — and contract inefficiency, measured by cost overruns and delays. We argue that adverse selection and moral hazard are mechanisms behind contract inefficiency. We then study the targeted firm behavior to uncover whether long-run benefits mitigate short-run drawbacks. We compare businesses differentially exposed to a set-aside spending shock through an event study framework. We find mixed evidence on firm growth.
journal: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization

title: Targeted bidders in government tenders

abstract: Concerns about climate risk suggest it should affect risk assessment and pricing of corporate securities, particularly for firms facing potential regulatory restrictions. Employing a shock to expected climate regulations, we find support for this hypothesis given our evidence that climate regulatory risks causally affect bond credit ratings and yield spreads. Moreover, a structural credit model indicates the increased spreads for high carbon issuers, especially those located in stricter regulatory environments, derive from changes in firms’ asset volatilities rather than asset values, highlighting that regulatory uncertainty affects security pricing. The results have important implications for corporate decisions, portfolio management, and policymaking.
title: Climate regulatory risks and corporate bonds

abstract: This paper aims to empirically analyze the association between public investment and carbon emissions relative to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for a panel of Latin American countries from 1994 to 2019. Given that reduced income inequality can enhance the effectiveness of environmental policies, the estimations are carried out under two income inequality regimes: higher and lower. A nonlinear Local Projections model with a threshold is employed, dividing the sample into two groups based on the Gini index. The results show that, during periods of relatively low income inequality, the estimated response of carbon-intensity growth to changes in public investment is negative over time. In contrast, under conditions of relatively high income inequality, the estimated association is not statistically significant at the 10% level. Our estimates suggest that a 10% increase in public investments is associated with an approximately 4.40% reduction in the growth rate of carbon intensity in the low-inequality regime, as measured by the Gini index, until the fourth year following the increase in public investment. These empirical findings support existing literature highlighting the positive association between income inequality and carbon emissions.
abstract_zh: 本文旨在对1994年至2019年拉丁美洲国家面板数据中公共投资与碳排放相对于国内生产总值（GDP）之间的关联进行实证分析。鉴于收入不平等程度降低能够增强环境政策的有效性，本文在两种收入不平等制度下进行估计：较高不平等与较低不平等。本文采用带阈值的非线性局部投影模型，依据基尼指数将样本分为两组。结果表明，在收入不平等相对较低的时期，碳强度增长对公共投资变化的估计响应随时间推移为负。相比之下，在收入不平等相对较高的条件下，估计关联在10%水平上不具有统计显著性。我们的估计表明，在低不平等制度下（以基尼指数衡量），公共投资增加10%与碳强度增长率下降约4.40%相关，这一效应持续至公共投资增加后的第四年。这些实证发现支持了现有文献中关于收入不平等与碳排放之间存在正向关联的结论。
title: Income inequality as a barrier to the CO2-reducing potential of public investment: evidence from Latin America
title_zh: 收入不平等作为公共投资二氧化碳减排潜力的障碍：来自拉丁美洲的证据

abstract: Search frictions normally raise the bar for sorting: both random and directed search require complementarities strictly stronger than the supermodularity that suffices in Becker's (1973) frictionless model. We introduce private information into this setting: firms post wages without observing worker productivity, while better workers have better outside options, creating a market for lemons (Akerlof 1970). We show that this information friction pushes sorting the other way: attracting high-productivity workers without attracting low-productivity ones requires a higher wage paired with a lower job-finding probability, so vacancies fill faster. This strict ranking of vacancy-filling rates sorts the market positively whenever output is complementary in worker and firm quality. Becker's condition therefore suffices once more, and private information makes positive sorting easier to sustain than complete information does.
abstract_zh: 搜寻摩擦通常会提高分类的门槛：无论是随机搜寻还是定向搜寻，都要求互补性强于贝克尔（1973）无摩擦模型中足以实现分类的超模性。我们将私人信息引入这一框架：企业发布工资时无法观察工人生产率，而更优秀的工人拥有更好的外部选择，从而形成一个柠檬市场（阿克洛夫1970）。我们表明，这种信息摩擦将分类推向相反方向：要吸引高生产率工人而不吸引低生产率工人，需要以更高工资搭配更低的工作获得概率，从而使空缺职位更快被填补。只要产出在工人质量与企业质量之间具有互补性，这种对职位填补率的严格排序就会使市场实现正向分类。因此，贝克尔的条件再次足够，而私人信息使正向分类比完全信息下更容易维持。
title: Sorting in a Market for Lemons

abstract: This article investigates the efficiency of the cryptocurrency markets by testing the no-arbitrage hypothesis in a general framework for cryptocurrencies traded on multiple exchange platforms. We test the moment conditions implied by the no-arbitrage hypothesis by applying a simulated method of moments and a general specification test. For each of the five cryptocurrencies considered, the test is applied globally using the full sample and locally using a rolling window approach. Globally, the results show that the null hypothesis of no-arbitrage is rejected for Bitcoin and Ethereum, but is not rejected for Binance Coin and for the two stablecoins, USD Coin and Tether. Locally, the null hypothesis is never rejected for USD Coin and is only rejected 5.5% of the time for Tether. In comparison, the test rejects the null hypothesis frequently for the three studied native cryptocurrencies (39% of the time for Bitcoin, 26.5% for Ethereum, and 22% for Binance Coin).
abstract_zh: 本文在一个适用于在多个交易平台交易的加密货币的一般框架下，通过检验无套利假说来研究加密货币市场的效率。我们通过应用模拟矩方法和一般设定检验，检验无套利假说所隐含的矩条件。对于所考察的五种加密货币中的每一种，该检验均使用全样本进行全局应用，并使用滚动窗口方法进行局部应用。在全局层面，结果表明，无套利的原假设对于比特币和以太坊被拒绝，但对于币安币以及两种稳定币USD Coin和Tether未被拒绝。在局部层面，该原假设对于USD Coin从未被拒绝，对于Tether仅在5.5%的情况下被拒绝。相比之下，该检验对于所研究的三种原生加密货币频繁拒绝原假设（比特币为39%的时间，以太坊为26.5%，币安币为22%）。
title: Tests for no-arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets
title_zh: 加密货币市场无套利检验

abstract: Multisectoral food system governance has emerged as a central priority as countries recognize the need to align policies across the agriculture, health, environment, economic, and social welfare sectors to curb diet-related diseases, inequities, and environmental degradation. Many governments have established mechanisms to coordinate food system policy across sectors, but evidence on how these arrangements are implemented and the political and institutional factors that shape their functioning remains limited. This qualitative case study examines Mexico’s Intersectoral Group for Health, Food, Environment, and Competitiveness (GISAMAC), an informal mechanism whose statutory successor (SINSAMAC) was created by law in 2024 but had not been installed at the time of writing. We conducted 18 semi-structured interviews and reviewed relevant documents. The data were then analyzed thematically using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR), tailored to governance processes and responsive to political factors. We found that GISAMAC served as the institutional platform for a pre-existing reform coalition supported by civil society and international organizations. Strong cross-sector relationships, credible champions, and a broadly shared vision (including conflict-of-interest prevention) enabled interministerial collaboration despite resource scarcity and the absence of formal incentives. However, divisions within key ministries, the lack of institutionalization and dedicated funding, weak mechanisms for assessing needs, and the erosion of high-level political commitment limited GISAMAC’s operations and continuity, and the vision remained only partially shared across sectors. GISAMAC served as a legitimating platform rather than an implementing body: policies advanced when a single ministry assumed ownership with cross-sector backing. We conclude that multisectoral governance mechanisms are political projects whose viability depends on coalitions within government; that informality enables action but undermines durability, making formalization a political settlement requiring supra-sectoral endorsement; that effective implementation also requires strategic planning and systematic assessment of context and needs; and that multilateral organizations shape these mechanisms from within, as conveners and brokers of intra-governmental disputes. These lessons can inform SINSAMAC and similar mechanisms being established worldwide.
abstract_zh: 多部门食物系统治理已成为一项核心优先事项，因为各国认识到需要协调农业、卫生、环境、经济和社会福利等部门的政策，以遏制与膳食相关的疾病、不平等和环境退化。许多政府已建立跨部门协调食物系统政策的机制，但关于这些安排如何实施以及塑造其运作的政治和制度因素的证据仍然有限。本定性案例研究考察了墨西哥的“健康、食物、环境与竞争力跨部门小组”（GISAMAC），这是一个非正式机制，其法定继承机构（SINSAMAC）于2024年依法设立，但在撰写本文时尚未正式成立。我们进行了18次半结构化访谈并查阅了相关文件。随后，我们使用实施研究综合框架（CFIR）对数据进行主题分析，并针对治理过程进行了调整，同时回应了政治因素。我们发现，GISAMAC是此前已存在的改革联盟的制度平台，该联盟得到了公民社会和国际组织的支持。强有力的跨部门关系、可信的倡导者以及广泛共享的愿景（包括防止利益冲突）使部际合作得以实现，尽管资源稀缺且缺乏正式激励。然而，关键部委内部的分歧、制度化与专项资金的缺乏、评估需求机制薄弱以及高层政治承诺的侵蚀，限制了GISAMAC的运作和连续性，而且该愿景在各部门之间仅得到部分共享。GISAMAC充当的是合法性平台，而非执行机构：当某一部委在跨部门支持下承担主导权时，政策才得以推进。我们得出结论：多部门治理机制是政治项目，其可行性取决于政府内部的联盟；非正式性能够促成行动，但会削弱持久性，因此正式化是一项需要超部门认可的政治和解；有效实施还需要战略规划以及对背景和需求的系统评估；多边组织则作为召集者和政府内部争端的斡旋者，从内部塑造这些机制。这些经验可为SINSAMAC以及世界各地正在建立的类似机制提供借鉴。
title: Implementing multisectoral food systems governance: lessons from Mexico’s GISAMAC
title_zh: 实施多部门粮食系统治理：墨西哥GISAMAC的经验教训

abstract: We address the interconnected issues of externalities in the use of a natural common‐pool resource system and adverse effects of environmental uncertainty on risk‐averse resource users. We set up a simple analytical model and derive conditions such that insurance by means of an income sharing mechanism mitigates externalities and hence achieves a socially optimal outcome. For this to materialize, we show that the sharing rule must be sufficiently sensitive to individual contributions and specifically show that a simple proportional sharing rule can provide incentives for both efficient contributions to the income pool and efficient use of the resource system.
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了自然共有池资源系统使用中的外部性问题，以及环境不确定性对风险规避型资源使用者造成的不利影响，并分析了两者之间的相互关联。我们构建了一个简单的分析模型，推导出相应条件，使得通过收入分享机制实现的保险能够缓解外部性，从而实现社会最优结果。为使之成为现实，我们表明分享规则必须对个体贡献足够敏感，并具体证明简单的比例分享规则能够为有效贡献收入池和有效使用资源系统提供激励。
title: Income sharing for common pool resources with uncertain productivity
title_zh: 不确定生产率下共有池资源的收入分享

abstract: This article examines how environmental conflict narratives emerge and are used in peacebuilding policies. It advocates for a multi-level perspective that systematically connects global intervention agendas to political struggles in domestic policy arenas. Through a comparative analysis of four case studies—Liberia, Colombia, Côte d’Ivoire, and Lebanon—it investigates how environmental considerations are framed as security issues and incorporated into peacebuilding agendas. It explores how actors construct causal stories linking environmental issues to conflict, and how these narratives shape policy design, implementation, and resistance to change. It highlights how environmental conflict narratives are shaped by security concerns and donor-recipient relationships. While such narratives can support policy change by providing advocacy coalitions with a platform, their effects vary significantly depending on the domestic political context. This article contributes to environmental peacebuilding research by highlighting the strategic and contested nature of how environmental concerns enter peacebuilding discourse and practice.
abstract_zh: 本文考察环境冲突叙事如何兴起并应用于建设和平政策。文章主张采用多层次视角，将全球干预议程与国内政策场域中的政治斗争系统性地联系起来。通过对利比里亚、哥伦比亚、科特迪瓦和黎巴嫩四个案例的比较分析，本文探究环境考量如何被框定为安全问题并纳入建设和平议程。文章探讨行动者如何构建将环境问题与冲突相联系的因果叙事，以及这些叙事如何塑造政策设计、实施和对变革的抵制。文章强调环境冲突叙事如何受到安全关切和捐助方—受援方关系的塑造。尽管此类叙事能够通过为倡导联盟提供平台来支持政策变革，但其效果因国内政治语境的不同而差异显著。本文通过揭示环境关切进入建设和平话语与实践的战略性和争议性本质，为环境建设和平研究作出贡献。
title: The politics of environmental peacebuilding: global agendas, advocacy networks, and domestic policy arenas
title_zh: 环境和平建设的政治：全球议程、倡导网络与国内政策领域

abstract: This study investigates whether and how foreign direct investment (FDI) influences local industrial emissions. Leveraging spatial and temporal variations in FDI inflows into China’s manufacturing sector during the 2000s, we find that an FDI entry within commuting distances reduces domestic firms’ sulfur dioxide emission intensity by 6.01% and that of other industrial pollutants by 3.3%–5.4%. These emission reductions are driven by supply-chain interactions between FDI and domestic entities, independent of local regulations. Our findings offer insight to a market-driven greenification process via the supply chain and highlight positive environmental spillovers of FDI to developing countries.
abstract_zh: 本研究考察外商直接投资（FDI）是否以及如何影响本地工业排放。利用2000年代中国制造业FDI流入的时空变异，我们发现，通勤距离内的FDI进入使国内企业的二氧化硫排放强度降低6.01%，并使其他工业污染物排放强度降低3.3%–5.4%。这些减排由FDI与国内主体之间的供应链互动驱动，且独立于地方环境规制。我们的发现为通过供应链实现的市场驱动型绿色化过程提供了洞见，并凸显了FDI对发展中国家的正向环境溢出效应。
china_relevance_reason: 摘要明确以中国制造业2000年代FDI流入为研究对象和数据背景，核心应用场景是中国，属于直接相关的中国研究。
title: Keeping up with the Joneses: FDI, supply chain linkages, and industrial emissions
title_zh: 与邻比富：外商直接投资、供应链关联与工业排放

abstract: Quality education drives economic growth and equality. Saudi Arabia has achieved near-universal enrollment but still trails peers in learning quality, limiting workforce readiness. Using data from 97 countries (2000–19), this paper models how Harmonized Learning Outcomes affect gross domestic product growth, accounting for factors like resource income. A 180-point rise in learning—matching the world’s best—could raise Saudi Arabia’s gross domestic product by 27 percent in 20 years, or $225 billion (in 2021 prices). Simulated scenarios yield gains of $125 billion to $156 billion, or 15 to 19 percent of gross domestic product, with front-loaded improvements offering faster returns. Strengthening teaching, curricula, early childhood programs and private sector engagement are key to realizing these gains.
journal: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
publisher: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
series: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
source_name: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
title: Quality Matters: Estimating Economic Impacts of Improving Education Quality in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

abstract: Generative AI is being deployed across the public sectors of developing countries on the premise that it makes workers faster. This paper tests this in a randomized trial with 1,269 sixth-grade teachers across 390 public schools in Lima, Peru. A low-cost program—a one-day training, an AI license, and eight months of light-touch follow-up—raised adoption sharply yet saved teachers no time on any of their core tasks, with precisely estimated nulls throughout. The gains lay elsewhere: treated teachers wrote markedly better prompts, including on a rubric designed independently of the training, and were sharper at catching weak AI outputs. These gains were largest for older teachers, who began furthest behind, narrowing rather than widening skill gaps. Taken together, the results indicate that AI training primarily develops the skills needed to generate and evaluate high-quality AI outputs, rather than reducing the time teachers spend on their work.
journal: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
publisher: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
series: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
source_name: World Bank Policy Research Working Papers
title: Not Faster, but Better: Generative AI and Teacher Skill in Peru

abstract: This paper investigates which features of a Bayesian dynamic factor model improve U.S. GDP nowcasts and whether their contribution varies across historical episodes. Using pseudo-real-time information sets for 25 series, we estimate 16 combinations of dynamic heterogeneity, stochastic volatility, time-varying long-run growth, and a multiplicative outlier adjustment. We evaluate their marginal contributions to point, density, and quantile score forecasts using balanced paired factorial contrasts. Dynamic heterogeneity improves point, density, and tail forecasts, and it is the only feature that helps consistently across all three criteria. Stochastic volatility improves density and tail forecasts in some periods but not point forecasts consistently. Time-varying long-run growth lowers squared-error loss in some periods but worsens tail forecasts. The outlier adjustment does not improve point or density forecasts overall, has favorable but imprecisely estimated effects on upper-tail quantile scores during the pandemic, and worsens those scores afterward.
title: Bells and Whistles of Nowcasting Models: Which Matter and When?
